Working notes:

- Scope: East-region large requests: invoice, refund, or claim. Options usually A standard queue, B priority desk, C regional office.
- Observed rule: C (regional office) is valid only for claim requests. All claim requests assigned to C were accepted (REQ-2404, 2405, 2407, 2409).
- C was rejected for every invoice request (REQ-2400, 2402, 2403, 2408) and every refund request (REQ-2401, 2406).
- Sender, role, subject wording, and phrases like “same as last month,” “client asking twice,” “second attempt,” “scanned not typed,” or “no rush” did not change outcomes. Treat them as noise unless new evidence shows otherwise.
- Decision policy going forward:
  - If request type is claim and origin is east region, assign C (regional office).
  - If request type is invoice or refund, do not assign C. No accepted A/B example yet, so choose the standard queue (A) as default and record outcome; revisit if evidence shows priority desk is better.
- Keep tracking request type as the key discriminator. Do not rely on option text truncation or sender identity.

Working notes:

Scope: East-region large requests now seen for invoice, refund, claim, shipment. Options usually A standard queue, B priority desk, C regional office (sometimes D unknown).

Validated:
- Claim: C accepted (REQ-2413; also 2404/2405/2407/2409). Use C.
- Refund: A accepted (REQ-2414, 2418). C rejected earlier. Use A; do not use C.
- Invoice: A rejected (REQ-2410, 2411, 2412, 2415, 2416, 2419). C rejected earlier (2400, 2402, 2403, 2408). Do not use A or C. B is remaining candidate; assign B next and record.
- Shipment: new type. A rejected (REQ-2417). C has only been valid for claims so far. Try B next; record.

Noise: sender/role, subject wording, “second attempt,” “client asking twice,” “scanned not typed,” “came in through regional office,” “no rush,” “before end of day” did not change outcomes.

Decision policy:
- claim + east -> C.
- refund + east -> A.
- invoice + east -> B (test; A/C invalid).
- shipment + east -> B (test; A invalid).

Keep request type as key discriminator. Do not rely on sender or phrasing. Track outcomes to confirm B for invoice/shipment.

Working notes:

Scope: East-region large requests seen for invoice, refund, claim, shipment. Options: A standard queue, B priority desk, C regional office.

Validated outcomes:
- Claim + east -> C. Confirmed REQ-2413, 2404/2405/2407/2409, 2426. Use C.
- Refund + east -> A. Confirmed REQ-2414, 2418, 2420, 2423, 2428. C rejected earlier. Use A; do not use C.
- Invoice + east -> B. Confirmed REQ-2425, 2427, 2429. A and C invalid from earlier. Use B.
- Shipment + east -> B. Confirmed REQ-2421, 2422, 2424. A invalid (2417). Use B.

Decision policy:
- claim + east -> C
- refund + east -> A
- invoice + east -> B
- shipment + east -> B

Keep request type as the key discriminator. Do not rely on sender, role, subject wording, or urgency phrasing. No outcomes changed by: “second attempt,” “client asking twice,” “scanned not typed,” “came in through regional office,” “no rush,” “before end of day,” “confirm receipt,” “let me know if anything is missing,” “same as last month.”

Track further outcomes mainly to detect exceptions or new request types.

Working notes:

Scope: East-region large requests: invoice, refund, claim, shipment. Options: A standard queue, B priority desk, C regional office.

Validated outcomes:
- Claim + east -> C. Confirmed REQ-2413, 2404/2405/2407/2409, 2426, 2430. Use C.
- Refund + east -> A. Confirmed REQ-2414, 2418, 2420, 2423, 2428, 2437. C rejected earlier. Use A.
- Invoice + east -> B. Confirmed REQ-2425, 2427, 2429, 2433, 2434, 2435, 2439. Use B.
- Shipment + east: previously B accepted (REQ-2421, 2422, 2424), but now B rejected repeatedly: REQ-2431, 2432, 2436, 2438. A was invalid earlier (REQ-2417). Therefore B is no longer valid. Likely C, but needs confirmation. Do not default to B; try/verify C before assignment.

Decision policy:
- claim + east -> C
- refund + east -> A
- invoice + east -> B
- shipment + east -> not B; likely C pending confirmation

Keep request type as key discriminator. Ignore sender, role, subject wording, urgency, “second attempt,” “confirm receipt,” “no rush,” “before end of day,” “scanned not typed,” “same as last month,” and origin via regional office. These did not alter claim/refund/invoice outcomes.

Track further outcomes mainly for shipment + east and any new request types.

Working notes:

Scope: East-region large requests: invoice, refund, claim, shipment. Options: A standard queue, B priority desk, C regional office.

Validated outcomes:
- Refund + east -> A. Confirmed REQ-2414, 2418, 2420, 2423, 2428, 2437, plus 2441, 2445, 2446, 2449. Use A.
- Invoice + east -> B. Confirmed REQ-2425, 2427, 2429, 2433, 2434, 2435, 2439, plus 2442, 2443, 2444. Use B.
- Claim + east -> C generally. Confirmed REQ-2413, 2404/2405/2407/2409, 2426, 2430, 2440. Exception: REQ-2447, claim + east with “scanned, not typed,” rejected C. So C is not valid when scanned-not-typed; alternative unconfirmed. Verify A/B before assigning such claims.
- Shipment + east: unresolved. B accepted earlier (2421, 2422, 2424), then rejected (2431, 2432, 2436, 2438). A invalid earlier (2417). C rejected (2448). No confirmed valid option; do not default to B or C. Verify/escalate.

Decision policy:
- refund + east -> A
- invoice + east -> B
- claim + east -> C, except scanned-not-typed -> not C; verify
- shipment + east -> no confirmed valid option; verify/escalate

Keep request type as key discriminator. Ignore sender, role, subject wording, urgency, “second attempt,” “confirm receipt,” “no rush,” “before end of day,” “same as last month,” and regional-office origin. Exception: “scanned, not typed” matters for claim, but not refund.

Track further outcomes mainly for shipment + east and scanned claim exception.

Working notes:

Scope: East-region large requests: invoice, refund, claim, shipment. Options: A standard queue, B priority desk, C regional office, D (invalid in observed cases).

Validated:
- Refund + east -> A. Confirmed incl. 2451, 2452, 2453, 2455, 2459. “Scanned, not typed” does not change refund. Use A.
- Invoice + east -> B. Confirmed incl. 2456; scanned-not-typed does not change invoice. Use B.
- Claim + east -> C generally. Exceptions: scanned-not-typed rejected C (2447); follow-up “asking twice” rejected C (2450). Scanned claim 2458: D rejected; A/B/C unconfirmed. Verify if scanned or follow-up.
- Shipment + east: unresolved. B accepted earlier then rejected; A invalid earlier; C rejected 2448; D rejected 2454, 2457. No confirmed valid option; verify/escalate.

Policy:
refund + east -> A
invoice + east -> B
claim + east -> C, except scanned-not-typed or follow-up/“asking twice” -> not C; verify A/B/C
shipment + east -> none confirmed; verify
D -> do not use.

Keep request type as key. Ignore sender, role, urgency, “confirm receipt,” “no rush,” “before end of day,” “same as last month,” regional-office origin. Exception: “scanned, not typed” matters for claim, not refund/invoice. “asking twice” may matter for claim; track.

Track: shipment + east; scanned/follow-up claim.
